stem: Who among the following were the critics of Swadeshi' movement and pleaded for a better understanding between the East and the West?
expl: Rabindranath Tagore’s political acumen exhibited a marked ambivalence. On the one hand, he denounced European imperialism, occasionally voicing full support for Indian nationalist. On the other hand, he also shunned the Swadeshi movement, denouncing it in his acrid September, 1925 A.D. essay “The Cult of the Chakra” (an allusion to elements of Gandhism and the Non-cooperation Movement). In addition, he viewed British control of India as a “Political symptom of our social disease.” Urging Indians to accept blind revolution but of steady and purposeful education.

stem: Who was the fi rst to suggest the boycott of British goods in Bengal?
expl: Krishna Kumar Mitra was an Indian freedom fi ghter, journalist, and leader of Brahmo Samaj. He was an active leader and was against the partition of Bengal. On 13 July, 1905 AD, In his Nationalist Bengali weekly Magazine titled ‘Sanjibani’ he boldly advocated for the freedom of the press. In his opinion, the manufacturing of British goods should be abolished. He called for a boycott of foreign goods, government offi cials and organisations by breaking all connections, people should mourn etc. His ideas were supported by a gathering in District Bagerhat (Division-Khulna) on 16 July, 1905 A.D.

stem: Boycott of British goods was adopted as a national policy in –
expl: Lord Curzon announced the partition of Bengal on July 20, 1905 A.D. As a result, Swadeshi Movement was announced in Townhall, Kolkata on August 7, 1905 A.D., and ‘Boycott Proposal’ was passed. The boycott of British goods was adopted as a national policy in this meeting.

stem: Who painted the famous image of Bharat Mata to visually associate the identity of India, as a Nation?
expl: To visually represent India as a nation, Abanindranath Tagore created the famous image of Bharat Mata (Mother India). This painting was made in 1905 A.D. during the Swadeshi Movement against the partition of Bengal. In the painting, Bharat Mata is depicted as a goddess with four hands, wearing a saffron-colored sari. Abanindranath Tagore’s portrayal of Bharat Mata became a symbol of nationalism and unity among Indians during the freedom movement.

stem:
Which of the following classes was mainly unaffected by the Swadeshi Movement of 1905?
(i) Women (ii) Farmers
(iii) Muslim (iv) Intellectuals
Select your answer from the following codes –
expl: On 20 July, 1905 A.D., Curzon issued an order for partitioning of Bengal. On 7 August, 1905 A.D., one of the fi rst mass protests was organized in Calcutta’s Town Hall, which was known as ‘Swadeshi Movement’. From this Movement, people started opposing the British offi ce, institute, and boycott foreign goods. A remarkable aspect of the Swadeshi Movement was seen in the active participation of women. To collect the public support, Aswani Kumar Dutt organized the committee which is known as (Swadesh Bandhav Society). Tilak, Lala Lajpat Rai and Aurobindo Ghosh played leading role in the fabrication of the Movement's character. In this Movement, women actively participated but farmers and Muslims were very limited involved in this Movement. They separated themselves from this Movement. Thus, option (c) is the correct answer.

stem: Vande Mataram became the theme song of the Indian National Movement during –
expl: During Swadeshi Movement, the actual day of partition, October 16, 1905 A.D., was declared a day of mourning throughout Bengal and the hearths in the houses were kept unlit. People tied rakhis on each other wrists as a symbol of brotherhood. In Calcutta, most of the offi ces were kept closed, and a strike was observed in some jute mills and railway workshops. The streets reverberated with Vande Mataram which became the overnight National Song of Bengal and later, the Theme ralley cry or anthem of the National Movement.

stem: The British journalist H.W. Nevinson was associated with:
expl: Henry Woodd Nevinson was a British journalist and was related to the Swadeshi Movement. Nevinson’s brief was to “discover the causes of the present discontent and to report, without prejudice the opinions of leading Indians as well as offi cials.” Nevinson travelled across India for four months, and his reports were carried by Manchester Guardian, Glasgow Herald, and Daily Chronicle. He re-edited these pieces into a book. 'The New Spirit in India'.

stem: Who among the following had founded the ‘Indian Society of Oriental Art’ to revive ancient art traditions of India?
expl: First Indian artist to gain international recognition, Abanindranath Tagore (which was initiated by E.B. Havell) was the principal artist and founder of ‘Indian Society of Oriental Art’. His elder brother Gaganendranath Tagore was also artists. He was a major exponent of Swadeshi values in Indian art and inspired the new life in Indian School of Art.
